pr_title: use options for custom polling rate for swiss public transport
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

Reintroduce the custom polling rate config which has been lost by the transition to `config_flow`. It still has `90s` as standard rate, but any internal can be configured now.

issue_context.title: Polling intervall changed since move to config flow?
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Ever since the migration to the new config flow setup, I reach the daily 1000 API hits limit around 3 pm whereas this had never happened before. I've already removed my two services and reconfigured them, but it didn't help. Therefore my question: has anything changed in the polling interval? I shouldn't be reaching 1000 hits a day.

Any info I can add to help figure this out? Debug logs, etc. I'm more than happy to provide.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.1.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2023.12

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Swiss public transport

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/swiss_public_transport/

### Diagnostics information

Unfortunately, when doing the maths, we end up saturating the rate limit quite fast.

Every `90s` a call means for one entry: `86400s / 90s = 960 calls`, therefore your result which shows saturation around 15h for two entries is correct. I am not sure, why and how this worked for you prior as nothing has changed in the logic of the update rate. It might have been, that something did not work right and now it does, but your result is the intended one at the moment.

I also think, a flat `90s` update rate might not be the best and there is a lot of room for improvement, like:

- Defining a relevant timespan of the entry: `ex. 7h - 18h`
- Letting one define a custom refresh rate for each entry: `ex. 180s`
- Having a dynamic refresh rate which is more precise when a connection is due soon: `ex. over 10min away --> 180s, below 10min --> 90s`
- just to name some, maybe you have more

What would you say about the options we have?

@joostlek This might be an interesting case for request frequency optimization. Do you know of other cases where this has already been implemented?

People can update their own update interval via disabling polling and using an automation with a service to setup polling. (Sounds like a hassle, but it also allows you to only poll when you are at area X or something like that, which could be useful, but that's different for everyone, hence its an automation).

Maybe set your default update interval to something comfortable with which you can setup 3-4 entries without hitting the limit.

> People can update their own update interval via disabling polling and using an automation with a service to setup polling. (Sounds like a hassle, ...

This indeed _IS_ a hassle.

More and more integrations are migrated from yaml configs to config flow, which I do get (though cannot agree with). If a feature from YAML is dropped by this migration it should be marked as a `breaking change`, because lets face it; it is.
What was once concisely defined and configured in one place now needs to be broken up over automations for each of these migrations and additional UI action is required.

It's great that the option to overrule and take more fine grained control over the polling using automations, but at least just keep an option in the UI that allows users to just set the polling interval as was the option back in YAML. This way the migration towards config flow can keep this interval during migration and no user changes are required.

I do agree that having an option to set the polling interval would be the easiest way to solve most people's difficulties with this. This is especially true for novices, of which more and more are starting to adopt HA. But I do understand that any integration is maintained on a voluntary basis, so it costs the devs their time.

I would however be more than happy to play around with an automation and disabled polling. Is there documentation somewhere on this? I'll do some searching later, but if you have something at the ready to point me in the right direction, I'd be very grateful.

This is not to be set on an integration specific level anymore and should be done by deactivating the polling for the integration and define an automation which updates the sensor. Deactivate the default sensor polling at `90s`: Automation for custom polling: ```yaml alias: SPT 3min polling description: "" trigger: - platform: time_pattern minutes: /3 condition: [] action: - service: homeassistant.update_entity target: entity_id: sensor.a_b_departure data: {} mode: single ```
We could propose to adapt the default interval to `180s` to have two entries work at the same time at least, which does seem ok for me.

Adding custom polling rates in the UI (also known as, scan interval) is no longer allowed.

If you wish to use a different interval, you can define your own, based on your own rules and schedule, using an automation that call the home assistant update entity service.
